variants.title: VASCULAR DUPLEX ULTRASOUND — ARTERIOVENOUS FISTULA (AVF) (NORMAL / MATURE FUNCTIONING STUDY)

blocks.x: CLINICAL INDICATION:
6-week post-operative maturation evaluation of a left radiocephalic arteriovenous fistula.
ANATOMIC SITE:
Left radiocephalic
TECHNIQUE:

High-frequency linear transducer (7.5–15 MHz) gray-scale, color Doppler, and pulsed-wave spectral Doppler sonography performed along the inflow artery, arteriovenous anastomosis, and venous outflow tract.
FINDINGS:
INFLOW ARTERY:
Artery Evaluated: Left radial artery.
Patency & Caliber: Patent with normal luminal diameter (4.2 mm), smooth walls, and no hemodynamically significant inflow stenosis.
Hemodynamics: Normal low-resistance monophasic forward flow (PSV = 135 cm/s, EDV = 78 cm/s).
Distal Runoff / Steal Assessment: Antegrade flow preserved in the distal artery beyond the anastomosis; no retrograde flow or arterial steal.
ARTERIOVENOUS ANASTOMOSIS / FISTULOUS COMMUNICATION:
Site & Patency: Surgical radiocephalic anastomosis, widely patent.
Anastomotic Diameter: 4.8 mm.
Doppler Velocity: Expected turbulent, high-velocity jet at the anastomosis (PSV = 260 cm/s) without focal narrowing.
DRAINING VEIN / OUTFLOW TRACT (FOR DIALYSIS AVF):
Outflow Vein: Arterialized left cephalic vein, widely patent and compressible.
Luminal Diameter: 6.8 mm (Maturation criteria: ≥ 6.0 mm).
Depth from Skin Surface: 3.5 mm (Maturation criteria: ≤ 6.0 mm).
Cannulation Segment Length: Straight, accessible segment measures 16 cm.
Volume Flow Rate (Brachial Artery / Outflow Vein): 840 mL/min (Maturation criteria: ≥ 600 mL/min).
Stenosis / Thrombus / Side Branches: No focal stenosis, intraluminal thrombus, or large competing collateral veins.
CENTRAL VENOUS OUTFLOW & SURROUNDING TISSUES:
Subclavian / Internal Jugular / Common Femoral Vein: Patent with normal cardiac pulsatility and respiratory phasicity; no central stenosis/occlusion.
Perivascular Tissues: No hematoma, seroma, lymphocele, or abscess.
IMPRESSION:
Mature, widely patent left radiocephalic arteriovenous fistula meeting all sonographic maturation criteria (diameter 6.8 mm, depth 3.5 mm, volume flow 840 mL/min).
Suitable for hemodialysis cannulation.

bank_title: VASCULAR DUPLEX ULTRASOUND — ARTERIOVENOUS FISTULA (AVF) — PHRASES BANK

bank.title: 1. Mature, Well-Functioning Hemodialysis AVF ("Rule of 6s" Met)

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: 6-week post-operative maturation evaluation of a left radiocephalic arteriovenous fistula.

subs.title: Findings
items: Inflow Artery: The left radial artery is patent, measuring 4.2 mm in diameter, with normal low-resistance monophasic flow (PSV = 135 cm/s, EDV = 78 cm/s).
Anastomosis: The radiocephalic anastomosis is widely patent (measuring 4.8 mm) with expected turbulent high-velocity flow (PSV = 260 cm/s) and no focal narrowing.

Venous Outflow: The arterialized left cephalic vein is widely patent and straight over a 16 cm segment in the forearm, measuring 6.8 mm in luminal diameter and 3.5 mm in depth beneath the skin surface. No focal stenosis, intraluminal thrombus, or large competing collateral veins are identified.
Volume Flow: Calculated mean volume flow in the distal brachial artery / proximal outflow tract is 840 mL/min.

subs.title: Impression
items: Mature, widely patent left radiocephalic arteriovenous fistula meeting all sonographic maturation criteria (diameter 6.8 mm, depth 3.5 mm, volume flow 840 mL/min).
Suitable for hemodialysis cannulation.

bank.title: 2. Juxta-Anastomotic Venous Stenosis (Most Common Dialysis AVF Failure)

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Poor blood flow rates and prolonged bleeding after needle removal in a right brachiocephalic AVF.

subs.title: Findings
items: Inflow & Anastomosis: The right brachial artery demonstrates abnormally elevated resistance for a dialysis circuit (PSV = 95 cm/s, EDV = 18 cm/s, RI = 0.81). The brachiocephalic anastomosis is patent.

Venous Outflow: Approximately 1.5 cm distal to the anastomosis (juxta-anastomotic swing segment), there is a focal, concentric intimal hyperplastic stenosis reducing the luminal diameter to 1.8 mm (compared to 6.5 mm in the adjacent normal cephalic vein). Spectral Doppler demonstrates marked focal velocity acceleration across the stenosis (PSV = 440 cm/s; PSV ratio = 4.6) with severe post-stenotic turbulence.
Volume Flow: Reduced brachial artery volume flow measuring 360 mL/min.

subs.title: Impression
items: Severe (> 75%) juxta-anastomotic stenosis of the right brachiocephalic arteriovenous fistula (PSV 440 cm/s, PSV ratio 4.6) resulting in reduced access volume flow (360 mL/min) and high-resistance inflow waveforms.
Interventional radiology / vascular surgery referral recommended for fistulogram and percutaneous transluminal angioplasty (PTA).

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Sudden loss of thrill and bruit in a left brachiobasilic arteriovenous fistula.

subs.title: Findings
items: Gray-scale imaging demonstrates complete occlusion of the left brachiobasilic anastomosis and the entire transposed basilic vein outflow tract by hypoechoic, non-compressible intraluminal thrombus extending up to the axillary vein confluence.
Color and power Doppler interrogation with low-velocity scale settings confirms complete absence of blood flow throughout the fistula tract.
The left brachial artery demonstrates high-resistance triphasic waveforms (PSV = 72 cm/s, EDV = 0 cm/s) consistent with loss of low-resistance runoff.

subs.title: Impression
items: Complete acute thrombosis of the left brachiobasilic arteriovenous fistula from the anastomosis to the proximal outflow tract.
Urgent vascular surgery / interventional radiology consultation recommended for mechanical thrombectomy / declotting.

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Cold, painful, numb right hand during hemodialysis sessions in a patient with a right brachiocephalic AVF.

subs.title: Findings
items: The right brachiocephalic AVF is widely patent with high volume flow measuring 1,450 mL/min.
Proximal to the anastomosis, the right brachial artery demonstrates markedly elevated, continuous antegrade flow (PSV = 215 cm/s, EDV = 140 cm/s).

However, distal to the anastomosis, the distal brachial, radial, and ulnar arteries demonstrate complete retrograde (reversed) systolic and diastolic blood flow directed toward the low-resistance fistula anastomosis, resulting in markedly dampened, low-amplitude monophasic waveforms at the wrist (radial artery PSV = 18 cm/s).

subs.title: Impression
items: Patent, high-flow right brachiocephalic arteriovenous fistula (1,450 mL/min) causing severe hemodialysis access-induced distal ischemia (steal syndrome), evidenced by retrograde flow in the distal brachial/forearm arteries.
Urgent vascular surgery evaluation recommended.

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Continuous machinery bruit and palpable thrill in the right groin 3 days after cardiac catheterization.

subs.title: Findings
items: At the level of the proximal right superficial femoral artery (SFA) bifurcation, a direct, short-neck fistulous tract (measuring 2.4 mm in width) communicates directly between the posterior wall of the proximal right SFA and the anterior wall of the adjacent right femoral vein.
Color Doppler demonstrates marked perivascular tissue vibration ("color bruit / confetti sign") centered at the communication.
Spectral Doppler reveals a continuous, high-velocity, low-resistance monophasic jet across the tract (PSV = 360 cm/s, EDV = 210 cm/s).
The right femoral and common femoral veins are dilated and demonstrate turbulent, pulsatile arterialized venous waveforms.
No associated pseudoaneurysm or DVT is identified.

subs.title: Impression
items: Iatrogenic post-catheterization arteriovenous fistula (AVF) between the proximal right superficial femoral artery and the right femoral vein with venous arterialization and perivascular tissue vibration.
Vascular surgery / interventional radiology consultation recommended for management.

subs.title: Clinical Indication
items: Pulsatile swelling and audible thrill in the medial left lower leg 10 days after a glass laceration.

subs.title: Findings
items: In the mid-medial left calf, a direct fistulous communication measuring 3.2 mm in diameter is identified between the left posterior tibial artery and one of the paired posterior tibial veins, surrounded by a resolving 1.8 cm perivascular hematoma.

Spectral Doppler demonstrates a turbulent, high-velocity, low-resistance jet across the fistula (PSV = 310 cm/s, RI = 0.36) with prominent arterialization of the proximal posterior tibial and popliteal veins.
Distal to the fistula, the posterior tibial artery at the medial malleolus shows mildly dampened monophasic flow (PSV = 32 cm/s).

subs.title: Impression
items: Post-traumatic arteriovenous fistula (AVF) between the mid-left posterior tibial artery and posterior tibial vein with proximal venous arterialization.
CTA runoff and vascular surgery / endovascular consultation recommended for stent-graft or surgical repair.
